cf.title: pg_upgrade: add --initdb option to create the new cluster automatically

input.subject: [PATCH] pg_upgrade: add --initdb option to create the new cluster automatically

verdict_reasoning: No level fails outright: reviewers took the goal seriously and worked on the design through v10. Two things still need agreement on the list before code review is useful. Daniel's in-tree versus wrapper doubt has no answer, and the thread does not show which failures remain once the docs-only 0001 is applied (maintenance-fit-2, already-exists-1). Heikki has not replied on the v9 cleanup design, which leaves --check able to keep a cluster on some failures (standards-compat-2) and adds a state-file contract between initdb and pg_upgrade (maintenance-fit-1).

brief.title: pg_upgrade --initdb option to create the new cluster automatically
brief.problem: Before pg_upgrade, users must run initdb by hand with settings that match the old cluster, mainly WAL segment size and data checksums. A mismatch shows up late, as a check_control_data() failure. The thread targets operators who run pg_upgrade directly, without a wrapper such as Debian's pg_upgradecluster.
brief.proposed_design: With --initdb, pg_upgrade reads WAL segment size and checksum setting from the old pg_control, briefly starts the old server to read template0 encoding, locale and ICU rules, and runs initdb in the target directory. Logs go to <new datadir>/pg_upgrade_output.d from the start, which a hidden initdb option allows. With --check, the new cluster is created, checked, then removed.
user_visible_surface: New pg_upgrade option --initdb-options, repeatable, with its own quoting rules, passed to initdb after the generated arguments.
Changed --check behaviour with --initdb: it creates a temporary cluster and removes it, along with separate WAL files.
New hidden initdb option --for-pg-upgrade=<state-file> that accepts a target holding only pg_upgrade_output.d.
Separate docs-only patch saying which initdb settings must match the old cluster when initdb is run by hand.
author_claims: Users get WAL segment size, checksums and locale wrong by hand and only find out at check_control_data().
pg_upgrade already reads the old control data, so doing this in-tree avoids having a wrapper rediscover it.
A parity script shows manual initdb plus pg_upgrade gives the same state as --initdb with the same options.
Failed checks clean up the new cluster, so the same command can be retried.
Reviewer Greg Sabino Mullane called it a much needed feature he would use a lot.
brief.thread_state: Reviewers Greg Sabino Mullane, Daniel Gustafsson, Hüseyin Demir, Heikki Linnakangas and Shihao Zhong drove the design through v10; Shihao gave an LGTM on v10. Heikki has not replied to the v9 design, and Daniel's doubt about in-tree versus wrapper was never settled; the CF entry needs a rebase.
unclear: Whether Heikki accepts the hidden initdb --for-pg-upgrade state-file design and the cleanup logic in v9 and v10.
Whether Daniel still prefers this in external wrappers, and whether the docs-only 0001 is still split out in v10.
How --initdb behaves with tablespaces and a separate WAL directory across retries.
Whether upgrades from version 10 work, since the v10 failure was left out of scope.
Whether copying daticurules into template0 follows the existing handling of locale settings.

prior_attempts.title: pg_upgrade documentation improvement
prior_attempts.quote: A better way to get the *cluster* locale is from pg_controldata.
prior_attempts.reason: Peter Eisentraut said the cluster locale is better taken from pg_controldata and doubted that pg_upgrade needs the encoding to match. The author asked whether to change the patch to use pg_controldata only, but no revised patch followed. Michael Paquier marked the entry returned with feedback because the thread had died.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P4 was a docs-only patch that told users to match encoding and locale from template0. Here the docs-only 0001 names only WAL segment size and checksums and points to pg_controldata, and the main patch automates the step.

objections.title: In-tree versus wrapper question is still open, and the scope has grown
objections.failure_scenario: Core takes on initdb orchestration, quoting of --initdb-options, temporary cluster creation and removal, and WAL directory emptying. Packagers who already ship pg_upgradecluster-style wrappers gain nothing. Every pg_upgrade user carries the extra failure modes in a tool whose failures happen during upgrade windows.
objections.argument: Daniel doubted that this complexity belongs in core (message #5) and asked for docs first (message #7). The author answered that pg_upgrade already reads pg_control (messages #6, #9), but Daniel did not reply on that point. Since then the patch grew from about 18 KiB to 73 KiB and added deletion and permission-restore logic. The docs-only 0001 fixes the stated problem, a late check_control_data() failure, with no new code.
objections.author_must_show: After 0001 documents the required settings, which users still get them wrong, and why can a wrapper not read pg_controldata as well?

critic.reasoning: Daniel's in-tree versus wrapper doubt got only "Maybe" in message #7, and the patch has since grown. P4 must not be used as support, and the runtime cost falls on --initdb users and maintainers, not on every pg_upgrade user.

objections.title: Manual initdb plus pg_upgrade --check already meets the need
objections.failure_scenario: An operator reads the WAL segment size and checksum state with pg_controldata and runs initdb by hand. If a value is wrong, pg_upgrade --check reports it within seconds, before any data is copied, and the operator reruns initdb. The project still carries a hidden initdb option, a state file and a second cleanup path to save that one retry.
objections.argument: Message #15 says only WAL segment size and checksums must match, since pg_upgrade copies encoding and locale. The docs-only 0001 states this and points to pg_controldata, and Daniel (message #7) and Shihao (message #17) want it applied on its own. The author's answer (messages #6, #9) is that pg_upgrade already reads pg_control. That shows the step is less convenient today, but it can still be done. The material has one reviewer's wish to use it (message #2) and no field reports measured against the improved docs.
objections.author_must_show: Once 0001 is applied, which concrete failures remain that pg_controldata plus pg_upgrade --check cannot catch before any data is copied?

critic.reasoning: Manual initdb with pg_controldata and --check can do the job, and message #15 narrows the required match to two settings. The thread shows one reviewer's wish and an older question, which does not show the need is common.

objections.title: --check with --initdb writes to disk and empties a WAL directory
objections.failure_scenario: A deployment script adds --initdb and then runs pg_upgrade --check in a pre-flight step, assuming it is read-only, as the current docs say. The check runs initdb, writes WAL into the directory named by --waldir, and then removes it. If shutdown or the state file fails, the docs say the cluster is retained, so the later real run fails on a non-empty target.
objections.argument: The v10 patch rewrites the --check description from "don't change any data" to "check clusters without performing the upgrade". With --initdb, the docs list several partial-cleanup outcomes that need manual recovery. Heikki asked that --check leave the target unmodified (message #24). The design meets that only on the success path, so --check now has failure modes that change files on disk.
objections.author_must_show: Can --check --initdb keep its guarantee in every failure case, for example by initializing into a throwaway location, so that --check never leaves files that block the real run?

critic.reasoning: The docs say cleanup also runs when checks fail, so "only on the success path" overstates it. But the cluster is retained when the state file cannot be read or shutdown is not confirmed, and Heikki has not replied to this design.

objections.title: Hidden initdb state-file protocol ties initdb internals to pg_upgrade cleanup
objections.failure_scenario: A later release adds an initdb option that creates storage outside the data directory, in the way --waldir does. Nobody updates the --for-pg-upgrade state file, so pg_upgrade --check --initdb leaves that storage behind. A retry then fails, or later cleanup removes the wrong thing, and operators find out in the field.
objections.argument: In v9 (message #25), initdb records the external WAL path, whether the directory existed before, its permissions and the nearest existing parent. pg_upgrade reads that record to empty WAL directories and restore permissions. This makes a private contract between two binaries, and v10 also touches src/common/rmtree.c and src/port/pgcheckdir.c. Heikki suggested the hidden option only to stop initdb rejecting pg_upgrade_output.d (message #24), and he has not replied on the cleanup design (message #25).
objections.author_must_show: What makes a future initdb option that creates external storage fail a test when it is missing from the state file and its cleanup?

critic.reasoning: Message #25 confirms the state file carries the WAL path, prior existence, permissions and parent for pg_upgrade's cleanup. Heikki proposed only the hidden option, and nothing in the thread makes a future external-storage option fail a test.

objections.title: --initdb-options adds a third argument-quoting grammar to pg_upgrade
objections.failure_scenario: An operator copies a working initdb command line into --initdb-options, with a quoted locale name or a Windows path such as --waldir=C:\pg wal. pg_upgrade splits it under its own rules for backslashes, quotes and newlines, which differ from both the shell and the -o/-O handling. The operator finds the mismatch only when initdb fails or builds the wrong cluster.
objections.argument: The v10 docs define a new tokenizer for --initdb-options: its own quote, backslash and newline rules. The existing -o/-O strings are passed through to pg_ctl under a different convention, and the thread already showed how fragile -O splitting is (message #8). Each new release would have to keep this grammar stable. A repeatable option that carries one initdb argument per use needs no grammar at all.
objections.author_must_show: Why not take one initdb argument per --initdb-options occurrence, so pg_upgrade never has to define or maintain its own quoting rules?

critic.reasoning: The v10 docs define pg_upgrade's own splitting and quoting rules for --initdb-options, and the option is already repeatable. The thread does not say why one initdb argument per use was not chosen.

refuted.title: Template0 ICU rules may differ between manual initdb and --initdb
refuted.failure_scenario: An old cluster has daticurules set on template0. One operator upgrades with manual initdb and another uses --initdb, both with the same options. If the v10 copy of daticurules runs only on the --initdb path, the two new clusters differ silently, and databases later created from template0 sort differently.
refuted.argument: In message #27, v10 copies template0.daticurules as a fix found in --initdb review (message #26). The material does not say whether plain pg_upgrade copies it too. The author's parity claim (message #25) rests on the two paths producing the same state. Template0 locale fields should be copied the same way in both modes, or the difference should be stated.
refuted.author_must_show: Does the daticurules copy run on every pg_upgrade path, and does the parity script cover an old template0 with ICU rules?

critic.reasoning: The scenario rests on an assumption that the copy runs only with --initdb, which the material does not support. Message #27 says "the upgrade now copies template0.daticurules", and how a manual initdb handles ICU rules is existing behaviour.

refuted.title: --initdb-options adds a second quoting grammar inside pg_upgrade
refuted.failure_scenario: Scripts start to depend on the documented quoting rules for --initdb-options. Those rules cover backslash before quote or space, adjacent quoted text, and newline rejection, and -O handles its string differently. A later fix to either grammar breaks those scripts, or the two conventions stay different in the same tool for good.
refuted.argument: The v10 docs define a custom tokenizer: quotes group text, single quotes are literal, and a backslash escapes only some characters. Greg found that hand-rolled splitting broke on quoted values with spaces (message #8). The fix was a new grammar, not reuse of an existing convention, and the docs do not say why the -O convention or a repeatable one-argument-per-option form would not work.
refuted.author_must_show: Why not make --initdb-options take exactly one initdb argument per use, so no quoting grammar is needed?

refuted.title: Packager wrappers already create the new cluster and own this policy
refuted.failure_scenario: A Debian site uses pg_upgradecluster, which already creates the new cluster. Its settings rules and the new --initdb rules can then differ, for example on group access, which v8 dropped (message #23), or on ICU rules, added only in v10. Users find the difference after the upgrade, when permissions or collations differ from what the other tool would have produced.
refuted.argument: Daniel asked in message #5 whether this belongs in external wrappers such as pg_upgradecluster, and message #7 answers only "Maybe". The brief lists that question as unsettled. Wrappers can read pg_control through pg_controldata, so core placement mainly saves them that call. The settings list kept changing during review: group access was added and then removed (messages #20, #23), and daticurules was added late (message #26). That suggests the policy is not settled enough to fix permanently in core.
refuted.author_must_show: What can --initdb do that a wrapper using pg_controldata and the 0001 docs cannot, and how would core and wrapper rules stay consistent?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-2. Its own scenario, that a wrapper and --initdb choose different settings, is not a failure of this proposal, and Heikki removed group-access inheritance to match manual initdb.

refuted.title: Remaining problem after the docs fix may not justify the added surface
refuted.failure_scenario: An operator who reads the 0001 docs runs pg_controldata, passes two flags to initdb, and runs pg_upgrade --check, which reports a mismatch before any data is touched. pg_upgrade and initdb maintainers still own a hidden initdb mode, a cleanup state file and a custom quoting grammar, and every future initdb option has to be weighed against them.
refuted.argument: The only field demand in the material is one reviewer who would use it (message #2), plus a pointer to an older question (message #1). Message #15 narrows the settings that must match to WAL segment size and checksums, both readable from pg_controldata, and 0001 documents them. Daniel's preference for wrappers such as pg_upgradecluster (messages #5, #7) was answered only by the author's argument that wrappers must rediscover data. Message #7 also proposed docs as the first step, and the v10 docs hunk is about 110 lines of option rules and failure modes.
refuted.author_must_show: Which users or tools still get the new cluster wrong once 0001's docs are applied, and why can a wrapper not cover them as pg_upgradecluster does?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of already-exists-1 for the docs-plus-manual point, and of maintenance-fit-2 for the wrapper point.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: pg_upgrade now creates and removes the new cluster and its separate WAL directory; no on-disk format changes.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The patch changes src/include/port.h, src/port/pgcheckdir.c and src/common/rmtree.c, which other frontend and backend code uses.

touch_points.label: psql UX conventions
touch_points.reason: No psql change, but pg_upgrade gains two options, a quoting grammar, and a --check that writes to disk.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: pg_upgrade removes directories and restores permissions from a state file, and passes user-supplied arguments to initdb.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: A hidden initdb option, a state file read by pg_upgrade, cleanup paths and a custom tokenizer need care in every release.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)
touch_points.reason: Message #5 asks whether this belongs in wrappers such as pg_upgradecluster, and the thread has not settled it.

questions: Once the docs-only 0001 is applied, which concrete failures remain that pg_controldata plus pg_upgrade --check cannot catch before any data is copied?
What can --initdb do that a wrapper reading pg_controldata cannot, given that message #15 narrows the required match to WAL segment size and checksums?
Can --check --initdb initialize into a throwaway location, so that a failed state-file read or unconfirmed shutdown never leaves files that block the real run?
What makes a future initdb option that creates storage outside the data directory fail a test when the state file and its cleanup do not cover it?
Why does --initdb-options not take exactly one initdb argument per use, so pg_upgrade needs no quoting rules of its own?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows both pg_upgrade and initdb would have to own it. Heikki Linnakangas shaped the hidden initdb option in message #24 but has not replied on the v9 and v10 cleanup design.
committability.liability: The owner signs for directory removal and permission restore during upgrades, the state-file contract between initdb and pg_upgrade, and the --initdb-options grammar, for as long as pg_upgrade supports these options.
committability.author_follow_up: The author produced ten versions in about four months in response to review. The CommitFest entry has needed a rebase since 2026-10-14.

priority.reason: The thread names the target users, operators who run pg_upgrade without a wrapper, but shows one reviewer's wish as demand. The v10 patch is 73 KiB across pg_upgrade, initdb, src/common and src/port, and its cleanup design and in-tree placement still lack agreement.

provisional_note: Without the code, two points could not be checked: whether --initdb-options reaches initdb without a shell, and whether the state-file-driven removal accepts only paths that pg_upgrade recorded. Only 3 of 28 messages were read directly.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_upgrade: Support for upgrading to checksums enabled
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets pg_upgrade run between clusters with different data checksum settings by rewriting page checksums while it copies files. The first version did this automatically in --copy mode, and a later version added an explicit --update-checksums option.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author closed the entry because reviewers showed little interest in the feature or in solving its remaining problems. One problem was still open: copyFile() has a separate Windows code path, and the author did not know how checksum rewriting should work there. He said the feature could not move ahead without an answer to it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm not sensing much enthusiasm for this feature or for working out the
remaining problems, so I'm closing this commitfest entry.

precedents_retrieved.title: add timing information to pg_upgrade
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds the elapsed time of each pg_upgrade step to the status output, for example "ok (took 82 ms)", formatted like psql's PrintTiming(). The goal was to show where upgrade time goes and to measure future work on reducing pg_upgrade downtime.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut questioned who besides developers would use the timings and said pg_upgrade output already has too much information that users cannot act on. He suggested that shell tools such as "pg_upgrade | ts" or "ts -i" are enough, and the author agreed to leave it at that unless someone saw a reason to build it in. Only a related fix that raised MESSAGE_WIDTH to 62 was committed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
If it's just for developers and expert users, perhaps existing
shell-level functionality like "pg_upgrade | ts" would suffice?

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_upgrade version and path checking
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set makes pg_upgrade check every executable it uses, require the new binaries to match pg_upgrade's exact major and minor version, and default --new-bindir to pg_upgrade's own directory. It came from Tom Lane's report that pg_upgrade 11.3 would use pg_dump 11.1.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut committed 0002 to 0004, which add the executable checks, the --new-bindir default and a typo fix. He found that 0001 compares pg_upgrade's version only with pg_ctl's, so it does not make all binaries match, and proposed a version check for each validate_exec() call instead. On 2019-09-02 the author said a new version would come that week, but no later version appears in the visible messages.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: It compares (new_cluster.bin_version != PG_VERSION_NUM), but new_cluster.bin_version is actually just the version of pg_ctl, so this is just comparing the version of pg_upgrade with the version of pg_ctl, which is not wrong, but doesn't really achieve the full goal of having all binaries match.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_upgrade documentation improvement
precedents_retrieved.summary: A documentation patch for pg_upgrade explained what "compatible initdb flags" means for the new cluster: the same encoding, locale and checksum settings as the old one. It told users to find the encoding and locale of template0 with psql -l and the checksum setting with pg_controldata.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut said the cluster locale is better taken from pg_controldata and doubted that pg_upgrade needs the encoding to match. The author asked whether to change the patch to use pg_controldata only, but no revised patch followed. Michael Paquier marked the entry returned with feedback because the thread had died.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
A better way to get the
*cluster* locale is from pg_controldata.

precedents_retrieved.title: Preserve versions of initdb-created collations in pg_upgrade
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make pg_upgrade preserve the recorded versions of collations created by initdb. In binary-upgrade mode, pg_dump would delete all initdb-created collations in the new cluster and dump CREATE COLLATION commands with version information, instead of updating the existing objects in place.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Review showed that the patch makes the pg_upgrade check fail for clusters initialized with SQL_ASCII encoding, where ICU collations for that encoding do not exist, and that it leaves the recreated collations looking like user-defined objects. The author then questioned the approach and suggested not creating collations in initdb at all. The reviewer replied that the problem would go away if the separate per-object collation version patch set were committed, since that drops the collversion column. The author then marked the patch Returned with Feedback without further changes.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think this problem goes away if we commit the per-object collation
version patch set[1].

precedents_retrieved.title: Backport perl tests for pg_upgrade
precedents_retrieved.summary: Backport the Perl TAP version of the pg_upgrade tests (commit 322becb60) and related follow-up commits to REL_13_STABLE and REL_14_STABLE, replacing test.sh there. The goal was zero dump differences in cross-version upgrade tests, so users would not need to compare dumps by eye.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier objected that the TAP tests were new development that took several tries to get right on HEAD, so backporting them risks a test bug that hides a critical pg_upgrade issue. He preferred to keep further work on HEAD only, and the author withdrew the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
If we were to backport
any of this, there is a risk of introducing a bug in what we do with
any of that, potentially hiding a issue critical related to
pg_upgrade.  That's not worth taking a risk for.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_upgrade: Pass -j option down to vacuumdb
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Peter Eisentraut, Michael Paquier, Tom Lane
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pg_upgrade pass its -j option to the vacuumdb commands in the generated analyze_new_cluster.sh script, so the post-upgrade analyze runs in parallel. Later versions added a VACUUM_OPTS variable to the script and a suggested vacuumdb --jobs command.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers held that pg_upgrade -j and vacuumdb -j are bound by different resources, so the same value should not be reused, and the generated script is meant to analyze gently. Tom Lane and Michael Paquier did not see most of the patch as better than the status quo and preferred a printed hint or a documentation-only change. The thread then moved to copying statistics in pg_upgrade instead.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: So based on that linking the value used by pg_upgrade and vacuumdb is a bad concept in my opinion, and the patch should be rejected.

precedents_retrieved.title: Rewriting the test of pg_upgrade as a TAP test
precedents_retrieved.summary: Replace the pg_upgrade test scripts, test.sh for Unix and the upgradecheck target in vcregress.pl for MSVC, with one TAP test. On MSVC the new test would run as part of bincheck.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut committed the basic TAP test, then reverted it because of a build farm issue and set the entry to Returned with feedback until there was a new plan. Two points were also still open: the patch removed the documented cross-version upgrade testing, and there was no plan for build farm animals that call vcregress.pl upgradecheck.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I have reverted this because of the build farm issue.  Putting the patch
on hold in the CF until we have a new plan.

The buildfarm client needs some adjustments first.

roaster_notes.note: No listed precedent records a reason that still applies here: P4's reason is answered by 0001, P1 concerns rewriting checksums during copy, and P9 has no recorded reason. Message #1 cites an earlier discussion with Jeff Davis about pg_upgrade running initdb itself, but the thread does not report how it ended.
The hidden initdb --for-pg-upgrade option follows existing practice for hidden binary-upgrade switches, so it was not raised. The docs-only 0001 has no compatibility impact.

The proposal changes no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog definition, wire protocol message or extension API; it runs the existing initdb before the existing pg_upgrade flow. The new persistent state (the initdb state file, the target and separate WAL directory cleanup) is paired with removal, and initdb's empty-directory rule limits what that removal can touch. The daticurules copy writes to the new template0 as existing locale handling does, which could not be confirmed without the code.

pg_upgrade and initdb run as the OS user that owns the clusters, and --initdb crosses no privilege boundary. The shell-injection risk in message #11 was fixed in message #15 with appendShellString(). Message #21 dropped group-access inheritance in favour of initdb's stricter default. No SQL-level privilege, RLS, or exposure surface is added. Two points depend on the code and could not be checked: whether --initdb-options reaches initdb without a shell, and whether the state-file-driven rmtree() accepts only paths that pg_upgrade itself recorded.
Not applicable; two objections are raised.
The problem is real and several reviewers engaged, but the demand evidence is one enthusiastic reviewer. The objection is 'show demand beyond the docs fix', not a rejection.
